plans.name: Hobby

plans.quote: $0 monthly plan fee. ... One-time $100 in usage credits. ... Up to 20 concurrently running sandboxes. ... Up to 1 hour per sandbox session. ... 10 GiB of sandbox storage, included.

plans.name: Pro

plans.name: Pro+ (600 concurrent)

plans.name: Pro++ (1,100 concurrent)

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.includedUsage: Custom deployment, pricing and billing; a $3,000 monthly minimum applies.
plans.quote: Custom deployment, pricing, billing, support, and limits. ... A $3,000 monthly minimum applies to Enterprise usage.

cpuBasisNote.value: Billed on the vCPU and RAM allocated, not on measured use; a running but idle sandbox pays the full rate.
cpuBasisNote.quote: The rate depends on how much compute the sandbox has allocated, not on how much it actually uses.

floor.value: Not applicable: billing is on allocation, so there is no measured-CPU floor.
floor.quote: The rate depends on how much compute the sandbox has allocated, not on how much it actually uses.

billingIncrement.quote: You pay per second for compute resources while your sandbox is running.

minimum.value: Not published. No minimum billed time or minimum spend is stated for Hobby or Pro; Enterprise has a $3,000 monthly usage minimum.
minimum.quote: A $3,000 monthly minimum applies to Enterprise usage.

perPlanDifferences.value: One published rate table applies to Hobby and Pro; Enterprise pricing is custom and not published. Pro's fee buys limits, not credits.
perPlanDifferences.quote: Upgrading to the Pro tier does not grant additional credits. It only increases the limits available to your project

compute.notes: Sandboxes can be configured with 1 to 8 vCPUs and 1 to 8 GiB of RAM. The pricing page says the default sandbox has 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB, while the billing FAQ says the default is 2 vCPU and 512 MiB; both pages are live and unreconciled. Paused and killed sandboxes are not billed.

defaultSize.value: Pricing page: default sandbox 2 vCPU / 4 GiB. Billing FAQ: default 2 vCPU / 512 MiB. Both are live and unreconciled.
defaultSize.quote: The default sandbox has 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB of RAM.
defaultSize.conflictQuote: Start with the default resources (2 vCPU, 512 MiB RAM)

disk.included: 10 GiB on Hobby, 20 GiB on Pro; storage is listed as free and included with every plan, with no per-GiB price published for exceeding the included disk.
disk.quote: | Disk | Included (10 GiB Hobby / 20 GiB Pro) | Included |

billedWhenStopped.value: No. Paused and killed sandboxes are not billed.
billedWhenStopped.quote: No. You only pay while a sandbox is actively running. Once a sandbox is paused, killed or times out, billing stops immediately.

snapshot.value: No separate snapshot storage price is published. The pricing page lists storage as Free; snapshots are not given their own line.
snapshot.quote: Sandbox storage is included with every plan at no extra cost.

volume.value: Not published. Volumes are in private beta and have no published price.
volume.quote: Volumes are currently in private beta.

egress.value: Not published. The published rate table has vCPU, RAM and Storage only; no egress or bandwidth price appears on the pricing page or billing docs.
egress.quote:
| vCPU | $0.000014 per vCPU-second |

deploy.oneClickOrManaged: Not found. There is no one-click or managed Hermes product; the closest is a pre-built E2B template.
deploy.officialTemplateOrGuide: Yes. E2B documents a pre-built hermes template and a page for running Hermes Agent, plus a separate OpenClaw gateway guide.
deploy.manualRoute: With the E2B CLI: run `e2b sbx create hermes`, then inside the sandbox run `hermes model` to configure a provider and `hermes` to start. Headless use is `hermes chat -Q --yolo ...` from the SDK. No Hermes terminal-backend integration is needed because Hermes runs inside the sandbox.
deploy.nonCoderDashboardOnly: No documented route. The Hermes page starts with the E2B CLI, and the alternative is SDK code with an API key; the console is documented for billing, templates and workspaces, not for running Hermes.

urls.quote: E2B provides a pre-built hermes template with the Hermes CLI and bundled skills already installed.
No separate Hermes terminal-backend integration is required for this setup.
Start the OpenClaw gateway in an E2B sandbox and connect your browser.
